psmith-in-the-city: Wodehouse's inimitable Psmith — monocle, charm, and effortless superiority — takes a job in a London bank, dragging his friend Mike along. Office drudgery meets Psmith's genius for elegant evasion in this early comic gem. The master's dialogue sparkles, and Psmith remains one of fiction's most delightful creations.
the-prince-and-betty: Wodehouse's comedy pairs a penniless prince with Betty, an American heiress, in a tangle of romance and mistaken identity. Set partly in New York, it shows the young master already wielding his light, sure touch. Charming early Wodehouse, full of sparkle and good humor.
sidelights-on-relativity: Albert Einstein himself explains relativity's sidelights — the ideas around his great theory — in these accessible lectures. The master popularizes his own revolution. Essential for all who wonder what it all means. Time, space, and light bend to his plain and playful explanations.
the-jewel-city: Ben Macomber celebrates the Jewel City — San Francisco's Panama-Pacific Exposition of 1915, a wonderland of palaces and lights. His account preserves the fair's magic. A glittering souvenir of a golden moment. Tower of Jewels and Palace of Fine Arts shine in his enthusiastic record.
